summary:
[  edit  ]
The Phaser  CHOP  does staggered (time-offset) animation interpolation. Phaser outputs one channel with multi-samples. Each sample animates from 0 to 1 over a cycle, but each sample value rises from 0 and arrives at 1 at different times.
For example, you may have a set of N objects that you want to animate from a start position to an end position. You set Num Samples to N, which will make the Phaser  CHOP  output one channel with N samples that will animate the samples from 0 to 1 and be interpolated with an easing function. In the Phaser  CHOP  the start-to-end cycle is controlled by the first input of the  CHOP , which is expected to be one channel with value between 0 to 1.
The 0-1 values can be used with the  Lookup CHOP  to animate groups of channels.
By default the timing is staggered uniformly.  If you want to stagger their transitions irregularly, you use the second input, a set of values in one  CHOP  channel (typically N samples) that are between 0 and 1. The phase value specifies the object's timing relationship with the rest of those in the  CHOP . A phase value of 1 corresponds to an animated object thats "ahead of the pack" (ie. it will start animating before the others). A value of 0 corresponds to an object that is late (ie. it will be the last to start easing/animating). If a phase input is not provided then the phase will simply be i/N where N is the total number of objects (ie. samples), and i is the index of the current sample.
There is also a notion of an "Edge" in the Phaser, which describes the cohesiveness of the group of animated objects and how fast the samples rise. A small value will cause the objects to go through the animation very quickly or at high value, very slowly and in unison with other samples.
Look at David Braun's   TouchDesigner Summit Talk   to see the background of the Phaser  CHOP . Its functionality draws heavily from David's research and development in quantitative easing.
See also the  OP Snippets .

inputs.description: Time  - The timing of the phase. When not wired the timing will default to an LFO ramp over 4 seconds. The  CHOP  should only contain one channel; all other channels except the first will be ignored.
Phase  - When wired the Phaser  CHOP 's output will mirror the phase input's. However, if Mult-Channel Output Format is selected it will in effect transpose the output.
Edge  - Edge samples will be used instead of the Edge parameter.

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: The separation edge of the phasing between two states. A smaller edge corresponds to sharper separation according to differences in phase. Edge Parameter will not be used if there is an Edge Input.

parameters.label: Num Samples
parameters.name: nsamples
parameters.description: Specify the size of the output. This parameter will not be used if there is a phase input.

parameters.label: Output Format
parameters.name: outputformat
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies the format of the output.

parameters.label: Multi-Samples
parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Multiple samples in a channel.

parameters.label: Multi- Channel
parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: Multiple channels.

parameters.label: Extend Input
parameters.name: extend
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies how the time input is interpreted to calculate the phaser value, if the time input is outside the 0-1 range.

parameters.label: Clamp
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: Time input clamped to 0-1 range.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: The phaser cycles the input time 0-1.

parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.name: mirror
parameters.description: The phaser Zig-Zags the input time between 0-1.

parameters.label: Mirror Slope
parameters.name: mirrorslope
parameters.description: The phaser Zig-Zags the input time between 0-1, with the slope of the phaser flipped.

parameters.label: Add
parameters.name: add
parameters.description: The phaser values keep on increasing (or decreasing) when the time input goes over 1 (or below 0).

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: Rename from
parameters.name: commonrenamefrom
parameters.description: The channel pattern to rename. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Rename to
parameters.name: commonrenameto
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the names. The default parameters do not rename the channels. See  Pattern Replacement .

parameters.label: Channel Names:  c[1
parameters.description: 10:2] ambient

parameters.label: Rename To:  b[1
parameters.description: 5] amb    This example fetches channels  c1 c3 c5 c7 c9  and  ambient .

parameters.label: num_channels

parameters.label: time_slice

parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame

parameters.label: warnings

parameters.label: errors

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

Experimental:Particle POP: Representa una partícula individual como un punto POP. Este operador añade opcionalmente atributos clave para sistemas de partículas como velocidad, dirección, edad, masa y fuerza. Es central para la simulación de partículas en TouchDesigner y genera atributos como PartForce. • Experimental:Pattern POP: Se utiliza para generar patrones para atributos, ofreciendo configuraciones más complejas. Permite crear y modificar atributos de color y textura. • Experimental:Phaser POP: Las fuentes proporcionadas no ofrecen una descripción detallada de la función específica de este operador. • Experimental:Point File In POP: Permite cargar archivos externos que contienen nubes de puntos en TouchDesigner, específicamente diseñado para este tipo de datos. • Experimental:Point Generator POP: Un operador generador que crea nubes de puntos directamente.
